claim: JUDGe's CFP explicitly and repeatedly states that negative results are welcome: 'Works in progress, negative results, practitioner case studies, and cross-disciplinary contributions are particularly encouraged' and again 'negative results, and works in progress are all welcome -- not just finished research.'
stance_target: Whether any NeurIPS 2026 workshop has an explicit stated position welcoming negative results
scope_conditions: JUDGe (Can We Trust the Judge?), NeurIPS 2026, Atlanta
quoted_support: Works in progress, negative results, practitioner case studies, and cross-disciplinary contributions are particularly encouraged — the workshop is designed for work that wouldn't fit neatly into a standard NLP or ML venue track.

claim: JUDGe's scope is specifically about reliability and validity of LLM-based evaluators/judges embedded in RLHF, DPO, and Constitutional AI pipelines -- not about search-loop feedback signals or NAS, creating a topical mismatch with the target paper despite its strong negative-results welcome.
stance_target: Topical fit of JUDGe for the target NAS paper
quoted_support: Judges embedded in RLHF, DPO, and Constitutional AI pipelines don't just mismeasure — their failure modes compound into model weights and downstream decisions.

claim: JUDGe submission tracks: Full Papers 6 pages + references (oral), Short Papers 4 pages + references (poster), Junior Spotlight 2 pages + references (oral, students/early-career only); double-blind, at least 3 reviews per paper; non-archival with author opt-out; previously published work at a major venue is explicitly not eligible; deadline Aug 29 2026, notification Sep 29 2026, camera-ready Oct 15 2026.
stance_target: Format, anonymity, archival status, and submission mechanics of this candidate venue
quoted_support: Full Papers 6 pages + references · Oral presentation / Short Papers 4 pages + references · Poster presentation / Junior Spotlight 2 pages + references · Oral · Students & early-career only ... All accepted work is non-archival and posted on the workshop website (authors may opt out). Previously published work at a major ML venue is not eligible.
